tactical.what_is_priced: The market prices Swedish sovereign risk at essentially zero and is correct to, but the relative pricing is where the krona benefit sits: in a month when gilts yield 5.04% and the German Bund reached a 15-year high, a AAA sovereign funding at 3.04% is a scarce asset. What is not priced is that a near-doubling of nominal bond issuance to SEK 220 billion this year, with the Riksbank holding only about SEK 20 billion and therefore out of the market, creates a large new supply of exactly that scarce asset at a yield 64 basis points higher than a year ago. That combination should attract reserve and real-money buyers, and buying krona bonds requires buying krona.

strategic.analysis: The strategic assessment keeps the Bullish stance but at slightly lower confidence, because the level is outstanding while the trajectory is the least favourable in Sweden's own modern history. On the level, the fiscal framework remains among the most disciplined in the world: a surplus target of one-third of one per cent of GDP over the cycle, an expenditure ceiling set three budget years ahead in nominal terms, and a 35% debt anchor with a formal requirement to report any deviation exceeding five percentage points of GDP. On the trajectory, three things are changing at once. The surplus target is being replaced by a balance target of 0% of GDP from 2027 following the Parliamentary Balance Target Commission's work. General government net lending is running at minus 2.6 to minus 2.7% of GDP in 2026, and Riksgalden forecasts budget deficits of SEK 196 billion in 2026 and SEK 208 billion in 2027, lifting central government debt from SEK 1,244 billion at end-2025 to SEK 1,430 billion at end-2026 and SEK 1,633 billion at end-2027, or 19% to 21% to 23% of GDP. And Maastricht debt rises from 34.6% in 2025 to 36.0% in 2026, 36.7% in 2027 and 37.9% by 2030 - which Riksgalden itself describes as approaching the upper limit of the range for the debt anchor while remaining low by international comparison. Crucially for how a currency market should read this, roughly two-thirds of the 2026 structural deterioration is the defence and Ukraine carve-out rather than discretionary domestic loosening: the Ministry of Finance's structural balance is minus 1.9% of potential GDP including new defence and Ukraine spending but only minus 0.6% excluding it. That spending is authorised under a cross-party agreement permitting a maximum SEK 300 billion increase in indebtedness over 2026-2034 with a commitment to return net lending to balance by 2035 at the latest. A pre-announced, ring-fenced, cross-party defence expansion in a 36%-debt AAA sovereign is not a credit event; it is a supply event, and supply events in high-quality government bond markets attract foreign capital. Confidence is 54 rather than higher because the 13 September election could add discretionary loosening on top of the carve-out.

strategic.what_is_priced: The bond market has priced the supply cleanly - a 64 basis point rise in the ten-year over twelve months and a 2s10s of plus 60 basis points against Germany's plus 39 - but it has priced it as a rates event rather than a currency event. The currency implication is the opposite sign to the fiscal headline: a near-doubling of AAA-rated krona bond supply, at a yield 64 basis points higher, with the central bank absent from the market, requires foreign absorption, and that absorption is krona demand. We think the market is treating Sweden's fiscal expansion the way it treats the United Kingdom's, which is a category error given a 36% debt ratio, a AAA rating and a legislated return to balance by 2035.

factors.horizon_split_explanation: Both horizons are Bullish and the stance does not change, but confidence falls from 57 to 54 as the horizon lengthens. Mechanically, the tactical case rests on things that are true today and cannot deteriorate within four weeks - three AAA ratings with Stable outlooks, 36% debt, no rating event scheduled, and smooth weekly auctions. The strategic case must additionally carry the trajectory, which includes the switch from a surplus target to a balance target in 2027, a Maastricht debt path rising to 37.9% by 2030, and a 13 September election whose outcome could add discretionary loosening on top of the ring-fenced defence carve-out. The level dominates on both horizons, but the strategic error bars are wider.

tactical.analysis: The structural configuration is unambiguously against the krona on both primary pairs, and it is unusually clean. USD/SEK moving averages are stacked in perfect ascending order - 200-day 9.3357, 100-day 9.4404, 50-day 9.5668, 20-day 9.6644 - which is the textbook signature of a currency in a sustained downtrend, and EUR/SEK replicates it exactly at 10.8554, 10.9191, 10.9839 and 11.0423. Spot at 9.51862 and 10.9783 sits below the two fastest averages and above the two slowest, which places both pairs in the middle of their ranges with the primary trend intact and the short-term momentum paused. For flow purposes this matters because systematic and trend-following capital keys off the 100-day and 200-day crossings, and spot is 2.0% above the USD/SEK 200-day and 1.1% above the EUR/SEK 200-day, so that capital is currently positioned against the krona and would need a 2% krona rally before it turned. The immediate structural obstacle for the krona is the USD/SEK 50-day at 9.5668, which capped the July pullback once already, with the 20-day at 9.6644 above it. On the volatility side the honest position is that the krona options surface is not observable: no free or public venue publishes one-month or three-month at-the-money implied volatility or 25-delta risk reversals for USD/SEK or EUR/SEK in mid-2026, so the variance risk premium cannot be computed and no risk-reversal figure is asserted anywhere in this dossier. Realised volatility is measurable and is decompressing: USD/SEK 20-day realised is 7.80% against 8.62% at 60 days and 9.87% at 120 days, and EUR/SEK 4.65% against 5.02% and 5.63%. Falling realised volatility inside an intact trend is the configuration most favourable to trend continuation, which for the krona means continuation lower. Confidence is capped at 56 because a third of this factor's required inputs are unobservable.

strategic.analysis: Across one to six months market structure remains a headwind for the krona, though a decaying one, and the assessment hinges on two specific prices. The 200-day moving averages at USD/SEK 9.3357 and EUR/SEK 10.8554 are the levels at which the strategic bullish thesis stops being a forecast and becomes a trend, because those crossings are where trend-following and CTA capital re-engages on the krona side. Spot is currently 2.0% and 1.1% above them respectively, so the fundamental case has real work to do before it gets structural support. The EUR/SEK 200-day at 10.8554 is the more important of the two, because it sits within four figures of the 10.8916 fair value implied by the real effective exchange rate deviation - a rare confluence of technical and valuation reference points that should make the 10.85 to 10.89 zone the most heavily contested area in the krona complex over the strategic horizon. Above spot, the 2026 highs at USD/SEK 9.7548 and EUR/SEK 11.0990 are the levels whose breach would invalidate the strategic view outright. The volatility regime supports a directional expression: realised volatility is decompressing across the complex, with USD/SEK falling from 9.87% at 120 days to 7.80% at 20 days, and low and falling volatility inside a trend historically rewards trend followers and penalises breakout traders. The krona nevertheless remains among the least liquid G10 currencies, and Swedish market participation is thinnest in July and early August, so the realised numbers understate the true tail. Confidence is 52, lower than the tactical 56, because over six months a fundamental repricing of the size implied by the fiscal unwind is entirely capable of breaking a moving-average structure, whereas over four weeks it is not.

strategic.what_is_priced: The moving-average structure prices six months of krona weakness as the prevailing regime, and nothing in the observable data contradicts it. The specific edge we identify is not in the vol surface, which is invisible, but in the confluence at EUR/SEK 10.85 to 10.89, where the 200-day average and the real-effective fair value coincide: a sustained break of that zone would simultaneously satisfy trend followers and valuation buyers, and is therefore likely to accelerate rather than mean-revert. We would treat a weekly close below 10.8554 as worth more than a comparable move on USD/SEK, because the euro cross isolates the Swedish story and costs only 37 pips a month to hold.

factors.horizon_split_explanation: Both horizons are Bearish because the moving-average stack is the same on both, but confidence falls from 56 to 52 as the horizon lengthens. The mechanism is that a technical structure is close to deterministic over four weeks - spot cannot traverse 2.0% to the USD/SEK 200-day and hold below it in that time without a shock - but is merely probabilistic over six months, during which the September and December Monetary Policy Reports and the lapse of the fuel duty cut on 30 November are all capable of forcing a break. factors.expression_assessment: The vol landscape cannot be characterised, and that conclusion is itself the expression recommendation. No free or public venue publishes one-month or three-month at-the-money implied volatility, IV percentiles or 25-delta risk reversals for USD/SEK or EUR/SEK in mid-2026, so it is impossible to say whether krona options are cheap or expensive, whether an event premium exists around the 20 August Riksbank Update or the 13 September election, or whether the market is hedging krona upside or downside. With the variance risk premium unmeasurable, buying options is a decision taken blind on price, and the correct default is spot. Realised volatility supports that default independently: USD/SEK 20-day realised at 7.80% is below both the 60-day at 8.62% and the 120-day at 9.87%, and EUR/SEK at 4.65% is below 5.02% and 5.63%, so actual moves are compressing inside an intact trend - the regime in which directional spot positions are rewarded and long-gamma positions bleed. Within spot, EUR/SEK is the efficient vehicle for the strategic bullish krona view because it costs only 37 pips a month in carry against 128 pips on USD/SEK, and carries 5.02% realised volatility against 8.62%, giving roughly three and a half times the carry-adjusted risk efficiency. For the tactical bearish view, NOK/SEK pays the holder 250 basis points a year to be positioned with the trend, which is the only krona cross where carry and structure agree. Position sizing should reflect that the krona's true tail is fatter than a 4.65% EUR/SEK realised number implies, because August is the thinnest month in the Nordic calendar and dealer spreads widen materially outside European hours.

tactical.analysis: Global dollar funding conditions are easy and getting easier, which is a tailwind for a small high-beta currency, but the dollar rate channel is simultaneously hostile, and over four weeks the two offset. On the supportive side, the Federal Reserve ended quantitative tightening on 1 December 2025 and has since been purchasing shorter-term Treasury securities to maintain an ample supply of reserves; total assets stood at 6,738,190 million dollars on 29 July, some 202 billion dollars above the 6,535,781 million trough of 3 December 2025, an increase of 3.1%. Reserve balances are around 3.1 trillion dollars and the Federal Reserve's own July 2026 Monetary Policy Report describes them as within the ample range and increased since early January. Secured overnight financing has been stable and well behaved: SOFR printed 3.65% on both 28 and 29 July after drifting up from 3.57% on 20 July, an eight basis point month-end move that is ordinary repo mechanics rather than stress, on daily volumes of 2.95 to 3.03 trillion dollars. There is no evidence of swap-line usage. On the hostile side, the policy rate itself is the problem: the effective federal funds rate at 3.63% sits 188 basis points above the Riksbank, the ten-year Treasury at 4.75% yields 171 basis points more than the Swedish ten-year, and the 29 July FOMC produced a 9-3 hold in which Hammack, Kashkari and Logan all dissented in favour of a 25 basis point increase - an unusually hawkish dissent structure that makes the next Fed move more likely up than down. The broad dollar index stood at 120.71 on 24 July and the DXY near 100.4 at month-end, so the dollar has drifted lower without breaking down. The unavoidable gap is that neither the three-month EUR/USD nor the JPY/USD cross-currency basis, nor any SEK/USD basis, could be sourced for mid-2026, so the standard measure of dollar funding premium is unobservable and confidence is capped at 57.

tactical.what_is_priced: The market prices ample dollar liquidity and a Fed on hold, and both are correct, so the funding channel offers no tactical edge on its own. The asymmetry that is not priced sits in the dissent structure: three regional presidents voting for a hike at a meeting where the committee held is a configuration that historically precedes a hawkish shift in the statement rather than a dovish one, and for a currency 188 basis points below the funds rate that is the wrong tail. We treat the liquidity tailwind and the rate tail as offsetting at 57% confidence, and note that the unobservable cross-currency basis means an emerging funding squeeze would be invisible to us until it showed up in spot.

strategic.analysis: Over one to six months the dollar liquidity picture stays constructive in level terms and unresolved in direction, which sustains the Neutral. The structural fact is that the global dollar tide has turned: the Federal Reserve is no longer draining reserves and has been adding to its balance sheet since December 2025, which historically improves the funding environment for small, illiquid, high-beta currencies of exactly the krona's type. If that continues, the krona is a disproportionate beneficiary, because its principal disadvantage in tight-dollar regimes is not its fundamentals but the width of its bid-offer. The counterweight is the dollar smile. Sweden sits at the worst point of that framework on both tails: in a risk-off episode the krona sells off on liquidity, and in a US-exceptionalism episode it sells off on rate differentials, so it needs the goldilocks middle - stable global growth, expanding European manufacturing, a gently softening dollar - to perform. That middle is currently in place, with the euro-area composite PMI at a five-month high of 51.9, German manufacturing flash at 52.2, credit spreads near three-year tights and the dollar drifting lower, but it is a narrow corridor and the Middle East conflict is capable of closing it. US inflation is the specific medium-term risk: core PCE at 3.3% and headline CPI at 3.5% are more than two percentage points above Swedish CPIF, and with three FOMC members already dissenting for a hike, a US tightening cycle resuming inside the strategic horizon would widen a differential that is already 188 basis points. Swedish banks carry moderate dollar funding needs through their Baltic operations, and the Riksbank maintains a dollar swap line whose usage would be a crisis signal, but no usage has been reported. The cross-currency basis remains unobservable across all three relevant pairs, which is the binding constraint on confidence.

strategic.what_is_priced: The market prices an ample-reserve, no-QT world in which dollar funding is a non-issue, and that is where the krona quietly benefits without anyone pricing it explicitly, because the liquidity premium a small currency pays is largest precisely when reserves are scarce. What is under-appreciated in the other direction is that the end of quantitative tightening removes the Federal Reserve as a marginal Treasury buyer at the same moment Sweden nearly doubles its own bond issuance, so both sovereigns are competing for the same real-money capital. We rate the net as balanced and record the factor Neutral, with the explicit caveat that an unobservable cross-currency basis means we would learn about a dollar funding squeeze from the exchange rate rather than from the funding market.

The tactical Neutral is a near-term standoff between observably easy funding conditions and a hawkish FOMC dissent structure. The strategic Neutral is broader: the same easing liquidity tide against the krona's structurally poor position on both tails of the dollar smile, plus the possibility of a resumed US tightening cycle on 3.3% core PCE. Confidence is marginally lower strategically because the corridor the krona needs - stable growth, expanding European manufacturing, a gently softening dollar - is narrow, and because the cross-currency basis that would give early warning is unobservable on both horizons.

weighted_score.interpretation: A net score of minus 0.161 is a modest bearish reading. It is produced almost entirely by Factor 1, which contributes minus 0.151 on its own from a Bearish stance at 63% confidence and a 0.24 weight, with smaller negative contributions from External Balance at minus 0.031, Market Structure at minus 0.028 and Event Risk at minus 0.025. The only positive contributions are Risk Appetite at plus 0.052 and Fiscal at plus 0.023. Four factors - Inflation and Growth, Flows, Guidance and USD Liquidity, together carrying 46% of the tactical weight - register Neutral and contribute nothing, which is why the score is modest rather than decisive: nearly half the framework is genuinely balanced and the bearish signal rests on the rate differential and the trend structure.
weighted_score.mapping_to_conviction: On the standard mapping, an absolute net score between 0.10 and 0.20 corresponds to conviction 2 of 5. Minus 0.161 sits in the upper half of that band but does not reach the 0.20 threshold for conviction 3. The mapping is corroborated qualitatively: the view depends on a single dominant factor rather than on broad factor agreement, the risk-reward is roughly 1.1 to 1, and two of the ten factors rest on data that does not exist.

tactical.rationale: At tactical weights the framework is dominated by Policy and Rates at 0.24 and Inflation and Growth at 0.18, which together carry 42% of the decision, and those two factors point in opposite directions with the rate factor winning. The Riksbank policy rate of 1.75% is the fourth lowest in the G10+SGD set and the third lowest in the G10 proper and produces negative carry against seven of ten peers, ranging from minus 50 basis points to the euro area and Canada out to minus 260 basis points to Australia, and the Swedish bond market corroborates rather than offsets that: the two-year at 2.44% yields 37 basis points less than the German Schatz and the ten-year at 3.04% yields 16 basis points less than the Bund. Over the next four weeks that differential can only widen, because the Riksbank's 20 August decision is a Monetary Policy Update that publishes no new rate path while the European Central Bank meets on 10 September with a market-implied hike probability of 77 to 83%. The Inflation and Growth factor is Neutral rather than supportive because the two sides genuinely cancel over a four-week window: Sweden posted the fastest growth in the European Union outside Ireland at 2.8% year-on-year and an Economic Tendency Indicator of 104.7, but the July CPI flash on 6 August and the full release on 13 August are the first prints to capture three new tax and subsidy cuts effective 1 July, so measured inflation should fall further from an already depressed CPIF of 1.3%. The factors reinforce each other in the wrong direction for the krona: the rate disadvantage, the deteriorating trade balance that compressed the June goods surplus to SEK 2.6 billion, and a moving-average structure stacked perfectly against the krona on both USD/SEK and EUR/SEK all push the same way. They conflict with Risk Appetite, where a VIX of 17.09, credit spreads near three-year tights and an OMXS30 whose twelve-month gain is vendor-reported near 21.5% and flagged should be helping a high-beta currency - and conspicuously are not, which is itself a warning. The edge we are expressing is not that Sweden is weak; it is that the market has four weeks of one-way news flow before the picture changes, and it is not positioned for that because krona positioning is unobservable. The path of least resistance is therefore higher on USD/SEK towards the 50-day at 9.5668 and the 20-day at 9.6644, and higher on EUR/SEK towards 11.00. The dated catalysts are the manufacturing PMI on 3 August, the CPI flash on 6 August, Norges Bank on 13 August with a live hike that would widen the Scandinavian carry deficit to 275 basis points, the full Swedish CPI on 13 August and the Riksbank Update on 20 August. What makes this more than a coin flip is that three of these five are scheduled data releases whose direction is largely known in advance because the underlying tax changes are legislated. Actionability is moderate rather than high: the view is expressible in spot, the cleanest vehicle is NOK/SEK where 250 basis points of carry pays the holder to be positioned with the trend, and the risk-reward of roughly 1.1 to 1 argues for modest size.

g10_ranking.commentary: The krona ranks ninth of eleven tactically because carry dominates a four-week horizon and the krona pays away carry to seven of ten peers, even though at 1.75% it is only the fourth lowest policy rate in the set. It beats only the yen, where the Bank of Japan is normalising into suspected intervention and a 40-year currency low, and the franc, where the Swiss National Bank is anchored at zero with an increased willingness to intervene. It loses most clearly to the krone, which combines a 250 basis point rate advantage with a 15.59%-of-GDP current-account surplus and a live hike on 13 August, and to the Australian dollar, which offers 260 basis points at only 5.11% realised volatility on the cross.

weighted_score.interpretation: A net score of plus 0.120 is a modest bullish reading built from three positive contributions and two negative ones. Guidance and Credibility contributes the most at plus 0.065 from a Bullish stance at 54% confidence on a 0.12 weight, followed by Inflation and Growth at plus 0.060 and Fiscal and Sovereign Risk at plus 0.038. The offsets are Event Risk at minus 0.028 and Market Structure at minus 0.016. Strikingly, five factors carrying 63% of the strategic weight register Neutral - Policy and Rates at 0.24, External Balance at 0.16, USD Liquidity at 0.12, Flows at 0.06 and Risk Appetite at 0.05 - so the entire strategic signal is generated by less than 40% of the framework. That is an unusual construction and it means the view is concentrated rather than broad-based.
weighted_score.mapping_to_conviction: An absolute net score between 0.10 and 0.20 maps to conviction 2 of 5, and plus 0.120 sits in the lower half of that band. The mapping is confirmed by the construction: with five factors and 63% of the weight registering Neutral, the signal comes from a narrow base, and the two largest strategic weights - Policy and Rates at 0.24 and External Balance at 0.16 - both contribute zero. Conviction 3 would require Policy and Rates to turn positively bullish, which is the single most important thing to monitor.

strategic.rationale: At strategic weights the framework shifts decisively: External Balance rises from 0.06 to 0.16 and Guidance from 0.07 to 0.12, while Inflation and Growth falls from 0.18 to 0.10 and Risk Appetite from 0.10 to 0.05. Policy and Rates remains the largest weight at 0.24 but turns Neutral, because the level of Swedish rates and their direction now offset. The core of the strategic bullish case is a single mechanical fact that is documented in the Riksbank's own June Monetary Policy Report and legislated in the Swedish statute book: temporary fiscal measures reduce CPIF by roughly 1.5 percentage points at their maximum in the third quarter of 2026, and the Riksbank's own CPIF excluding those measures runs at 2.0% for 2026, exactly at target, against a headline of 1.1%. Those measures expire on a known schedule - the fuel duty reduction on 30 November 2026, the halved public transport passes on 31 December 2026 and the food VAT cut in January 2028 - and the Riksbank's own forecast accordingly has CPIF rising from 1.1% to 1.7% in 2027 and 2.8% in 2028, with CPI reaching 3.4%. Against that, its published rate path adds only 12 basis points in 2026 and 17 in 2027. That internal inconsistency is the edge, and it must be resolved at the 24 September Monetary Policy Report, when the board publishes a new path for the first time since June. The factors that reinforce it are Guidance, where the Riksbank has already declared its risks skewed to the upside and its credibility is confirmed by Prospera five-year expectations at 2.1%, and Fiscal, where a AAA sovereign at 36% debt is nearly doubling bond issuance to SEK 220 billion with the central bank holding only SEK 20 billion, creating a large new supply of scarce high-quality krona assets that must be absorbed by foreign buyers. The factors that conflict are Event Risk, where the 13 September election, the Section 301 tariff track and the Hormuz situation are all live, and Market Structure, where spot sits 2.0% above the USD/SEK 200-day. The path of least resistance is lower on EUR/SEK towards the 200-day at 10.8554, which coincides with the 10.8916 real-effective fair value. The dated catalysts are the 24 September Monetary Policy Report, the 13 September election, the 30 November fuel duty expiry, the 26 November Riksgalden borrowing report and the 17 December Monetary Policy Report. What makes this more than a coin flip is that the inflation step-up is arithmetic rather than forecast. Actionability is good: short EUR/SEK costs only 37 pips a month in carry against 128 on USD/SEK, and carries 5.02% realised volatility against 8.62%.

consensus_divergence.consensus_view: The consensus is for gradual krona appreciation through 2026 towards fair value, with the Riksbank on hold or hiking once. The National Institute of Economic Research forecasts EUR/SEK averaging 10.86 and USD/SEK 9.34 in 2026 with the KIX index appreciating from 119.7 to 117.1, the Riksbank's own forecast assumes a further slight strengthening of the krona and its published path adds 12 basis points in 2026, Danske Bank forecasts hikes at both the September and December meetings to 2.25% while recommending a long USD/SEK position with a 9.80 target, ING expects no Riksbank hike at all in 2026 with a EUR/SEK year-end target reported at 10.70, and Trading Economics' model has USD/SEK at 9.68 for the third quarter and 9.44 in twelve months.
consensus_divergence.our_view: We agree with the direction over six months and disagree sharply on the timing and the reason. We are more bearish than consensus over the next four weeks, with a base case of USD/SEK 9.65 against a consensus clustered near 9.30 to 9.45, because the market has not priced the fact that three separate tax and subsidy cuts took effect on 1 July and will depress the 6 and 13 August CPI prints. Over one to six months our base case of USD/SEK 9.20 and EUR/SEK 10.82 is close to the National Institute's numbers, but we get there through a different mechanism and with a different rate view: we expect 50 basis points of Swedish tightening by mid-2027 against a published path implying about 20.
consensus_divergence.divergence_magnitude: Roughly 25 to 35 ore of USD/SEK on the tactical horizon, where we are more bearish the krona than almost anyone, and roughly 30 basis points on the 2027 Swedish rate path, where we are more hawkish than the Riksbank's own published curve. On the primary pair the six-month divergence is small in level terms but large in path terms.
consensus_divergence.why_we_differ: The market is reading a CPIF print of 1.3% as an economic fact when the Riksbank has publicly stated it is depressed by roughly 1.5 percentage points of temporary tax cuts, and is reading a 2.8% growth rate as noise when the Economic Tendency Indicator at 104.7 and the manufacturing PMI at 58.3 both corroborate it. Two specific things are being underweighted. First, the expiry schedule is legislated, not forecast: the fuel duty reduction lapses on 30 November 2026, the halved transport passes on 31 December 2026 and the food VAT cut in January 2028, and the Riksbank's own forecast has CPIF rising from 1.1% to 1.7% to 2.8% across those dates while its path adds only 29 basis points to end-2027. Second, the manufacturing PMI input price index at 81.3 against a 57.8 historical average and producer import prices up almost 10% in March and April represent a genuine cost-push pipeline that is entirely independent of tax policy. Consensus is also, in our view, over-extrapolating a six-month energy shock in the trade data while ignoring that Sweden exported a net 33.98 terawatt-hours of electricity in 2025 and its mineral fuels and electric current export line is up 33% year-on-year.
consensus_divergence.payoff_if_right: The tactical divergence is worth roughly 20 to 35 ore on USD/SEK over four weeks, or about 2 to 3.5%, from a position that also earns 128 pips a month of carry. The strategic divergence is worth more: if the September Monetary Policy Report revises the path higher and the market reprices 2027 Swedish tightening from 20 to 50 basis points, the Swedish-German two-year spread should narrow from minus 37 basis points towards minus 15, and EUR/SEK should trade through the 10.8554 confluence towards 10.65 to 10.75.
consensus_divergence.risk_if_wrong: If consensus is right that the krona appreciates gradually from here, the tactical short is wrong by about 1.25% and loses in the first fortnight of August, which is a small and quickly identifiable error. The more expensive way to be wrong is strategic: if the Riksbank genuinely looks through the mechanical inflation step-up - the position Jansson and Hjelm argued in the June minutes - while the European Central Bank reaches 2.75% by early 2027, the differential widens to 100 basis points and EUR/SEK trades to 11.30 or beyond, a 3.8% loss on the strategic long with no carry compensation. That scenario carries a 25% probability in our framework.

cleanest_bullish_expression.rationale: The euro cross isolates the Swedish story from the dollar cycle and is by a wide margin the cheapest way to be long the krona: only 50 basis points of negative carry, worth 37 pips a month against 128 pips on USD/SEK, and 5.02% sixty-day realised volatility against 8.62%, giving roughly three and a half times the carry-adjusted risk efficiency. The fundamental contrast is favourable in a way the market is not pricing: Sweden grew 2.8% year-on-year in the second quarter against the euro area's 1.0%, and Sweden's inflation undershoot is artificial while the euro area's 2.9% flash HICP is real. The technical target is the 200-day at 10.8554, which sits within four figures of the 10.8916 real-effective fair value.

cleanest_bearish_expression.rationale: The Scandinavian cross combines the widest durable carry the krona faces at 250 basis points, worth roughly 251 pips a year on a spot of 1.00394, with the strongest external contrast in the set: Norway runs a 15.59%-of-GDP current-account surplus against Sweden's 4.5%, and Norway is the direct beneficiary of the same Brent and TTF shock that is compressing Sweden's goods surplus. Norges Bank meets on 13 August with explicit guidance that the rate will likely be raised at one of the forthcoming meetings, which would take the differential to 275 basis points. The caveat is valuation: the krona is 5.82% cheap to the krone on a real-effective basis and the cross is already 8.55% higher over six months, so this is a trade to hold rather than to chase.

Carry has won for six months, so this is a contrarian position that requires the strategic Swedish repricing to work, and it should be sized smaller than the euro cross.

A way to fade the krona's least reliable positive carry. cross_horizon_consistency.summary: The horizons diverge cleanly: tactically Bearish at minus 0.161 with conviction 2, strategically Bullish at plus 0.120 with conviction 2. This is a timing divergence, not a disagreement about the underlying economics.
cross_horizon_consistency.divergence_explanation: The divergence is mechanical and dated rather than analytical. Every krona-negative element in the tactical assessment is a scheduled event inside the next four weeks - the 6 and 13 August CPI prints that capture three tax cuts effective 1 July, a 20 August Riksbank Update that publishes no new rate path, a 10 September European Central Bank meeting carrying a reported 77 to 83% hike probability, and a live Norges Bank meeting on 13 August. Every krona-positive element is a scheduled event beyond it - the 24 September Monetary Policy Report with a new path, the 30 November lapse of the fuel duty reduction, the 31 December lapse of the transport subsidy. Three factors change stance between the horizons: Policy and Rates moves from Bearish to Neutral as the level disadvantage is offset by directional optionality, Inflation and Growth from Neutral to Bullish as the fiscal distortion reverses, and Guidance from Neutral to Bullish as the Riksbank is forced to publish new paths.
cross_horizon_consistency.inflection_point: 24 September 2026, the Riksbank's next full Monetary Policy Report and the first new rate path since June. A secondary inflection sits at 13 September with the general election, and a confirming one at 30 November when the fuel duty reduction lapses.
cross_horizon_consistency.catalyst_for_transition: The Riksbank being forced to reconcile a published rate path that adds 12 basis points in 2026 and 17 in 2027 with its own inflation forecast showing CPIF rising from 1.1% to 1.7% and CPI from 0.6% to 2.7%. That reconciliation cannot be deferred past 24 September, and we put a 55% probability on the path being revised higher.
cross_horizon_consistency.trading_implication: Trade the two horizons as separate positions rather than netting them. The tactical short krona is best expressed in NOK/SEK, where 250 basis points of carry pays the holder to wait, and should be sized to a two-to-four-week horizon with a stop above NOK/SEK 1.02. The strategic long krona is best expressed in short EUR/SEK, built into weakness towards 11.10 rather than at spot, with the 200-day at 10.8554 as the confirmation level and the 2026 high at 11.0990 as the invalidation.

edge.6m: -2,434 pips on USD/SEK (forward 9.44337, we expect 9.20) and -1,361 pips on EUR/SEK (forward 10.95607, we expect 10.82). The six-month edge of 2,434 pips is 2.56% of USD/SEK spot and 1.24% of EUR/SEK spot, and is the quantified expression of the strategic bullish krona view.

forward_vs_spot.interpretation: Traded krona forward points were not obtainable from a free public venue, so the forwards above are derived by covered interest parity and are stated as derived rather than quoted. The Swedish leg uses STIBOR three-month at 2.04% as fixed on 29 July 2026; the dollar leg uses SOFR at 3.65% on 29 July; the euro leg uses an estimated three-month Euribor of 2.45%, because the last sourced Euribor fixing of 2.31% dates from 5 June 2026, before the European Central Bank's 25 basis point hike on 17 June, and the post-hike level is an estimate carrying roughly plus or minus 10 basis points of uncertainty. Because Sweden yields less than both counterparts at the front end, both pairs trade below spot in the forwards - the forward market already implies krona appreciation of 1.6% annualised against the dollar and 0.4% against the euro, which is simply the mechanical signature of a low-yielding funding currency and not a forecast. The structure of our edge is therefore unusual and worth stating plainly: at one month we expect the krona to underperform its own forward by 1,441 pips on USD/SEK, at three months the sign flips, and at six months we expect it to outperform by 2,434 pips. That shape is the forward-market expression of the same tactical-bearish, strategic-bullish divergence that runs through the whole dossier, and it argues for selling the krona forward at one month and buying it at six rather than holding a single directional position across both.

key_catalysts.event: Swedbank/Silf Sweden Manufacturing PMI, July 2026
key_catalysts.rationale: The June reading was 58.3, above the 54.3 historical average for a full year, with new orders the largest positive contributor. Because 1 August 2026 fell on a Saturday the July print publishes on the first banking day, Monday 3 August. A reading holding above 57 would confirm that Swedish manufacturing is expanding despite the euro-area energy shock and would support the strategic growth case.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced - the market focus in the first week of August is entirely on the CPI flash, and the PMI has been a consistent upside surprise for twelve months
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/SEK most directly, because the manufacturing channel is how Swedish growth transmits to the krona against the euro; secondarily NOK/SEK

key_catalysts.event: Statistics Sweden CPI flash estimate, July 2026
key_catalysts.rationale: The first print to capture three measures effective 1 July: a further temporary reduction in fuel duty running to 30 November, a 50% cut in public transport monthly passes running to 31 December, and lower preschool and after-school fees. CPIF was 1.3% in June and CPIF excluding energy 0.4%, and all three measures push the July number lower. We expect CPIF near 1.0 to 1.2%.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially - the market knows the reforms exist but has not, in our view, sized their combined effect on a single month's print
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/SEK and USD/SEK equally; the krona typically moves 0.3 to 0.5% on a 0.2 percentage point CPIF surprise

key_catalysts.event: Reserve Bank of Australia policy decision
key_catalysts.rationale: The RBA is expected to hold at 4.35% with an explicit tightening bias after 75 basis points of hikes in 2026 and trimmed-mean inflation at 3.6%. A hold with hawkish guidance keeps the widest carry deficit the krona faces at 260 basis points and reinforces the relative-carry case against AUD/SEK.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Fully priced as a hold; the guidance tone is not
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: AUD/SEK, the widest negative carry cross for the krona at 260 basis points

key_catalysts.event: Norges Bank policy decision
key_catalysts.rationale: Norges Bank raised to 4.25% on 6 May and its June guidance stated the policy rate will likely be raised at one of the forthcoming meetings, with a published path running just above 4.50% at end-2026. A hike would take the krona's Scandinavian carry deficit from 250 to 275 basis points with NOK/SEK already above parity at 1.00394 and up 8.55% over six months.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially - market pricing sits near even odds after the 15 July CPI-ATE print of 2.7% came in soft
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: NOK/SEK, the cleanest tactical expression of the bearish krona view

key_catalysts.event: Statistics Sweden full Consumer Price Index, July 2026
key_catalysts.rationale: The full release gives CPI, CPIF, CPIF excluding energy, HICP and the new CPIF-XE constant-tax series, which is the cleanest read through the fiscal distortions. It also carries Statistics Sweden's explanation of the July change in the air-fare data source. A CPIF print below 1.2% with CPIF excluding energy below 0.4% would make a September Riksbank hike materially less likely.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially - the flash on 6 August will have set the level, so the market reaction will hinge on the composition and on the constant-tax series
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/SEK primarily; the Riksbank's target variable is CPIF and EUR/SEK is the cross it watches

key_catalysts.event: Eurostat full July 2026 HICP for the euro area
key_catalysts.rationale: The flash showed headline 2.9% and core excluding energy, food, alcohol and tobacco at 2.5%, with energy at 10.0% against 8.5% in June and services at 3.3%. Confirmation at those levels keeps the European Central Bank's September hike probability above 75% and widens the expected policy differential against the krona from 50 towards 75 basis points.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Largely priced from the flash; a core revision above 2.6% would not be
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/SEK, the dominant krona axis

key_catalysts.event: Riksbank monetary policy decision (Monetary Policy Update)
key_catalysts.rationale: The meeting is on 19 August with the decision announced on 20 August and applying from 26 August. It is an Update rather than a full Report, so no new rate path is published until 24 September. The June path implies 1.77% at this meeting, and the June minutes showed three of five board members - Jansson, Hjelm and Bunge - effectively arguing for leaving the path alone, so a dovish tone is more likely than a hawkish one.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Fully priced as a hold; we put the probability of a hawkish surprise below 20% and of a mildly dovish tone at roughly 45%
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/SEK and NOK/SEK; the Scandinavian cross would react most because Norges Bank meets a week earlier

key_catalysts.event: Statistics Sweden foreign trade in goods, July 2026
key_catalysts.rationale: June showed exports of SEK 197.9 billion, up 11.7% year-on-year, against imports of SEK 195.3 billion, up 18.1%, leaving a surplus of only SEK 2.6 billion against SEK 13.3 billion a year earlier. With Brent up roughly 23% during July and TTF gas up 38%, the July import bill should be higher again and the surplus could turn negative for the first time in years.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced - monthly Swedish trade data is not a mainstream market event, which is precisely why a first deficit print would be a genuine surprise
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/SEK and NOK/SEK; the Norwegian comparison is stark given Norway's 15.59%-of-GDP surplus

key_catalysts.event: Statistics Sweden full national accounts, Q2 2026
key_catalysts.rationale: The 29 July indicator showed 1.4% quarter-on-quarter and 2.8% year-on-year but carries no expenditure detail. The full accounts give the composition - household consumption, investment, exports and inventories - for the first time. If the strength is domestic demand rather than inventories or net trade, it materially strengthens the case that the output gap is closing faster than the Riksbank's minus 0.8% assumption.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced - the headline is already public, so the market has not focused on the composition
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/SEK, given the euro area grew only 0.4% quarter-on-quarter in the same period

key_catalysts.event: Reserve Bank of New Zealand and Bank of Canada policy decisions
key_catalysts.rationale: The RBNZ is expected to hike 25 basis points to 2.75% after raising in July and saying further increases appear likely, while the Bank of Canada is expected to hold at 2.25% for a seventh consecutive meeting. The two roughly cancel for the krona: the New Zealand gap widens from 75 to 100 basis points against it, while the Canadian gap stays at 50.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Both largely priced; the RBNZ guidance is the variable
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: NZD/SEK and CAD/SEK, both second-order crosses for the krona

key_catalysts.event: Statistics Sweden balance of payments, Q2 2026
key_catalysts.rationale: The first quarter showed a current-account surplus of SEK 93.9 billion against SEK 131.3 billion a year earlier, with investment income accounting for SEK 21.2 billion of the SEK 37.4 billion fall and goods for SEK 14.1 billion. The second quarter captures the full energy shock, so a further deterioration towards SEK 80 billion is likely and would put the four-quarter average below 6% of GDP.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced - quarterly Swedish balance of payments is a low-profile release
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/SEK on the strategic horizon; the external balance carries a 0.16 strategic weight

key_catalysts.event: European Central Bank policy decision with updated staff projections
key_catalysts.rationale: The deposit rate was raised to 2.25% effective 17 June 2026 and the reported probability of a further 25 basis point increase in September is 77 to 83%, flagged as second-hand commentary rather than a sourced OIS print, with markets fully pricing 2.75% by early 2027. A hike takes the policy differential against the krona from 50 to 75 basis points at a meeting where the Riksbank has published no new path since June.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Largely priced at 77 to 83%; the staff projections and the guidance on the path beyond September are not
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/SEK, the single most important cross for this dossier

key_catalysts.event: Swedish general election - all 349 Riksdag seats, plus municipal and regional elections
key_catalysts.rationale: Elections are held on the constitutionally fixed second Sunday of September on a four-year cycle. The fiscal framework is cross-party and the June 2025 rearmament agreement authorising up to SEK 300 billion of additional debt for defence over 2026-2034 was reached across party lines, so the framework itself is not at stake. What is at stake is the 2027 Budget Bill and whether an incoming government adds discretionary loosening on top of the ring-fenced defence carve-out with the structural balance already 1.9% of potential GDP below target.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced - Swedish elections historically generate little exchange-rate risk premium, which is itself a source of asymmetry if this one is different
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/SEK; a fiscally expansionary outcome would be read through the bond market first, via the SGB-Bund spread

key_catalysts.event: Federal Open Market Committee policy decision
key_catalysts.rationale: The 29 July meeting held at 3.50-3.75% by 9 votes to 3, with Hammack, Kashkari and Logan all dissenting in favour of a 25 basis point increase against core PCE of 3.3% and headline CPI of 3.5%. A hold with the same dissent structure is neutral for the krona; a hike would widen the dollar differential from 187.5 to 212.5 basis points and is the largest single tail risk to the strategic bullish view via USD/SEK.
key_catalysts.priced_in: A hold is priced; the three-vote hawkish dissent structure is not fully reflected in the distribution of outcomes for later meetings
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: USD/SEK, which carries the krona's second-widest carry deficit and the highest realised volatility of any krona cross at 8.62%

key_catalysts.event: Riksbank monetary policy decision with full Monetary Policy Report and a new rate path
key_catalysts.rationale: This is the single most important date in the dossier and the inflection point between the tactical and strategic views. It is the first new rate path since June, and the board must reconcile a path that adds 12 basis points in 2026 and 17 in 2027 with its own inflation forecast showing CPIF rising from 1.1% to 1.7% and CPI from 0.6% to 2.7%. We put a 55% probability on the path being revised higher and a roughly 40% probability of a 25 basis point hike at this meeting.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially - the market prices at least 25 basis points for 2026 as a whole but treats the June path as stable rather than as a document that must be revised
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/SEK above all; a higher path would compress the Swedish-German two-year spread from minus 37 basis points towards minus 15

key_catalysts.event: Riksbank monetary policy decision (Monetary Policy Update)
key_catalysts.rationale: The June path implies 1.83% at this meeting. It falls three weeks before the fuel duty reduction lapses on 30 November and after two further CPI prints, so it is the meeting at which the board can pre-signal a December move without publishing a new path. Danske Bank forecasts hikes at both September and December, so a November signal would validate the more hawkish end of the forecast distribution.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced as a live meeting; the market focus is on September and December
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/SEK and SEK/CHF, the latter because a Riksbank hike would widen the krona's best carry from 175 to 200 basis points

key_catalysts.event: Riksgalden Central Government Borrowing report 2026:2
key_catalysts.rationale: The May report raised the 2026 budget deficit forecast to SEK 196 billion and 2027 to SEK 208 billion, and lifted nominal bond issuance from SEK 118 billion in 2025 to SEK 220 billion in 2026 and SEK 240 billion in 2027. The November update is the first to incorporate the post-election fiscal picture. More issuance is a fiscal negative but also a larger supply of AAA krona assets at a yield 64 basis points higher than a year ago, which requires foreign absorption.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced - the report publishes at 09:30 and is a bond-market rather than a currency event, which is why the currency implication is under-analysed
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/SEK via the SGB-Bund spread, currently minus 16 basis points at ten years

key_catalysts.event: Expiry of the temporary reduction in Swedish fuel duty
key_catalysts.rationale: The carbon dioxide tax reduction on petrol and diesel introduced from 1 May and extended from 1 July lapses on 30 November 2026. The Riksbank estimates fuel duty cuts worth up to 0.5 percentage points of CPIF. The December CPI print, published in January 2027, is the first to capture the reversal, and it is the earliest hard evidence that the mechanical inflation step-up is real.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced - expiry dates of temporary tax measures are legislated facts that FX markets systematically ignore until the data prints
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/SEK; this is the first of the two scheduled expiries that drive the strategic bullish case

key_catalysts.event: Riksbank monetary policy decision with full Monetary Policy Report
key_catalysts.rationale: The June path implies 1.87% at this meeting, and Danske Bank's house forecast carries a 25 basis point hike here to 2.25% following a September move, flagged as a forecast-table figure. It is the last decision inside the strategic window and the first at which the board can observe the fuel duty expiry taking effect. A hike would take the policy differential against the euro area from 50 basis points to 25 or less, depending on ECB action.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially - a December move is the modal expectation in the sell-side distribution, with Goldman Sachs explicitly expecting the first hike no earlier than December
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/SEK and NOK/SEK; a December hike would begin closing the Scandinavian carry deficit for the first time this cycle

key_catalysts.event: Expiry of the 50% reduction in Swedish public transport monthly passes
key_catalysts.rationale: The temporary state grant enabling regions to halve the price of 30-day public transport tickets runs from 1 July to 31 December 2026. Statistics Sweden reports that monthly passes are 44% of the combined passenger transport subclass and confirms the measure is treated as an indirect effect and is NOT stripped out of the constant-tax series, so its reversal will show up directly in January 2027 CPI.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced - the same systematic blind spot that applies to the fuel duty expiry
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/SEK; the January 2027 CPI print lands inside the strategic window's tail

If Jansson and Hjelm's look-through argument prevails and the path is unchanged, the mechanism converting the fiscal unwind into krona strength is removed and the krona reverts to being simply a low-yielding currency with no offsetting policy story.

invalidators.monitor_frequency: Quarterly, at each full Monetary Policy Report

invalidators.mechanism: Sweden's June goods surplus was already compressed to SEK 2.6 billion with imports up 18.1% year-on-year, and the National Institute assumes Brent at 90.2 dollars for 2026. A sustained move above 100 dollars would push the goods balance into deficit, cut the current account below 4% of GDP and simultaneously damage euro-area industrial demand, which takes roughly half of Swedish exports.
invalidators.monitor_frequency: Daily, assessed on a four-week rolling average

invalidators.condition: The European Central Bank raises its deposit rate to 2.75% by the December 2026 meeting while the Riksbank remains at 1.75%
invalidators.mechanism: This would widen the policy differential from 50 to 100 basis points and drag the Swedish-German two-year spread from minus 37 basis points towards minus 60, mechanically lifting EUR/SEK through the 2026 high at 11.0990. It is the specific combination that ING's forecast of no Swedish hike in 2026 implies.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: ECB deposit facility rate and Riksbank policy rate
invalidators.monitor_frequency: At each ECB and Riksbank decision
invalidators.quantitative_threshold: ECB 2.75% with Riksbank at 1.75%, a 100 basis point gap

invalidators.condition: The 13 September general election produces a government that announces discretionary fiscal loosening beyond the ring-fenced defence carve-out, taking forecast Maastricht debt above 40% of GDP
invalidators.mechanism: Maastricht debt is forecast at 36.0% of GDP in 2026 and 37.9% by 2030 against a 35% anchor with a five-percentage-point reporting tolerance. Breaching 40% would exhaust that tolerance and convert Sweden's fiscal position from a krona asset into a krona liability, particularly with nominal bond issuance already scheduled to rise to SEK 240 billion in 2027.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: Ministry of Finance Maastricht debt forecast in the 2027 Budget Bill; SGB-Bund 10-year spread
invalidators.monitor_frequency: At the Budget Bill and monthly thereafter
invalidators.quantitative_threshold: Forecast Maastricht debt above 40% of GDP, or the SGB-Bund 10-year spread turning positive by more than 20 basis points

invalidators.mechanism: The July flash composite at 51.9 was a five-month high and German manufacturing at 52.2 beat a 50.1 consensus; the krona's principal growth channel is European industrial demand operating with roughly a one-quarter lag. Two months back below 50 would remove that channel and confirm that the energy shock has broken euro-area activity, which historically produces krona underperformance regardless of the Swedish domestic picture.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: HCOB euro-area composite PMI, flash and final
invalidators.monitor_frequency: Monthly, flash around the 24th and final in the first week

factors_changed.reason: The June dossier was written on 17 June, the day the Riksbank announced its hold and raised its path, and treated the policy gap as balanced. Six weeks later the European Central Bank's 25 basis point hike effective 17 June has been fully absorbed and a September follow-up carries a reported 77 to 83% probability, flagged as second-hand, while the Riksbank's next decision on 20 August is a Monetary Policy Update that publishes no new path. The differential is now on a widening trajectory rather than a balanced one.

The prior dossier read the June path revision as an unambiguous strategic positive. This dossier separates the level from the direction: the level disadvantage has widened as the ECB, RBNZ and Norges Bank all tightened while the Riksbank held, and the June minutes published on 24 June revealed that three of five board members effectively argued for leaving the path alone. Direction and level now offset.

The growth side improved, with Q2 GDP at plus 2.8% year-on-year and the Economic Tendency Indicator rising to 104.7, but the inflation side deteriorated: CPIF fell from 1.5% in May to 1.3% in June and CPIF excluding energy from 0.5% to 0.4%, and three further tax and subsidy cuts took effect on 1 July that will depress the 6 and 13 August prints. The two sides now cancel over a four-week horizon.

The bullish flow case rested on the structural krona-buying of the buffer funds' hedge books. This dossier gives equal weight to the offsetting position - AP7's SEK 1,500 billion, explicitly unhedged and dollar-financed - and notes that the foreign ownership share of Swedish government bonds is not published, so the absorption of the near-doubled issuance programme cannot be tracked.

factors_changed.factor: 5: External Balance & Terms of Trade - tactical
factors_changed.reason: This is the largest single change and it is data-driven. Brent has risen from roughly 79 dollars in mid-June to about 88 dollars, having traded near 95 dollars intra-month on vendor data, flagged, and Dutch TTF gas is up 38% on the month. The June trade release showed imports up 18.1% year-on-year against exports up 11.7%, compressing the goods surplus to SEK 2.6 billion from SEK 13.3 billion a year earlier, and the Q1 current account fell SEK 37.4 billion year-on-year.

factors_changed.factor: 5: External Balance & Terms of Trade - strategic
factors_changed.reason: The stock remains excellent, with a net international investment position of plus SEK 4,033 billion and a current-account surplus still the third largest in the set, but the flow is now clearly deteriorating on a defined path from 5.8% of GDP in 2025 to a forecast 4.7% in 2026 and 4.3% in 2027, with the Riksbank expecting net trade to subtract from GDP growth in both years.

The prior dossier had access to the 17 June statement but not to the minutes, which were published on 24 June and were materially more dovish than the report. Jansson described a wait-and-see approach as the best strategy and was sceptical of insurance hikes; Hjelm judged second-round effects insignificant and said the March path remained reasonable. The 20 August meeting is also an Update with no new path.

In mid-June a United States-Iran memorandum of understanding had just been announced and Brent had collapsed to about 79 dollars. That agreement subsequently broke down, the blockade was reimposed, and Iranian forces stopped two tankers in the Strait of Hormuz in late July. In addition, the 13 September general election has moved from six months away to six weeks away, and the United States tariff regime has hardened through Section 122 and the Section 301 investigations.

In mid-June the moving-average configuration was tangled. It is now perfectly stacked against the krona on both primary pairs - USD/SEK 200-day 9.3357 below the 100-day 9.4404 below the 50-day 9.5668 below the 20-day 9.6644, with EUR/SEK identical - and spot sits 2.0% and 1.1% above the respective 200-day averages, so systematic flow is positioned against the krona.

The stance is unchanged and the ratings are unchanged at AAA across all three agencies, but confidence is lower because the trajectory has become clearer: Riksgalden's 28 May report lifted the 2026 budget deficit forecast to SEK 196 billion and nominal bond issuance to SEK 220 billion, Maastricht debt is forecast at 36.0% of GDP rising to 37.9% by 2030, and the surplus target is replaced by a balance target from 2027.

The cross is now 1.1% above its 200-day average of 10.8554 rather than below it, so the technical backdrop has deteriorated even as the fundamental case for a fiscal-unwind repricing has strengthened.

signposts_triggered.implication: Confirmed on the thesis-positive side. Swedish manufacturing is expanding through the European energy shock, and the input price index at 81.3 against a 57.8 average adds a cost-push element the prior dossier did not have.

signposts_triggered.signpost: German manufacturing PMI, previous level 49.0 in June 2026 described as a 34-month high
signposts_triggered.outcome: Rose to 52.2 on the July flash against a 50.1 consensus, with the output sub-index at 54.7, a 53-month high
signposts_triggered.implication: Decisively confirmed. Germany takes 10.1% of Swedish goods exports and is the transmission channel for the krona's industrial beta. This is the single most thesis-positive signpost outcome of the period and has not yet shown up in the exchange rate.

signposts_triggered.signpost: CPIF excluding energy year-on-year, previous level 0.5% in May 2026
signposts_triggered.outcome: Fell to 0.4% in June 2026; the confirming threshold in the prior dossier was a rise, so this outcome was thesis-negative
signposts_triggered.implication: The measured undershoot deepened rather than reversed, and three further tax and subsidy cuts took effect on 1 July that will depress the July print further. This is why Factor 2 moves to Neutral tactically even as it strengthens strategically.

signposts_triggered.signpost: Brent crude, previous level approximately 79 dollars on 16 June 2026 after the announced agreement
signposts_triggered.outcome: Rose to about 88 dollars by 31 July, up roughly 23% during July alone with a wide vendor-reported intra-month range of roughly 70 to 95 dollars, flagged as best available
signposts_triggered.implication: Clearly invalidating for the external-balance leg of the prior thesis. The June memorandum of understanding collapsed, the Hormuz blockade was reimposed and tanker attacks resumed, driving the terms-of-trade deterioration that compressed the June goods surplus to SEK 2.6 billion.

signposts_triggered.signpost: SGB-Bund 10-year spread, previous level approximately minus 12 basis points
signposts_triggered.outcome: Widened modestly to minus 16 basis points, with the Swedish 10-year at 3.04% and the Bund at 3.20% on 31 July; both yields rose, the Bund to a 15-year high
signposts_triggered.implication: Marginally thesis-negative but less than the headline suggests, because the Swedish 10-year rose 33 basis points on the month and touched 2.98% on 21 July, its highest since November 2023. Sweden is repricing higher alongside Germany rather than lagging it.

signposts_triggered.signpost: VIX, previous level approximately 16.2 on 15 June 2026
signposts_triggered.outcome: 17.09 on 30 July after a one-session spike to 20.66 on 29 July; credit spreads widened only five to eight basis points at the peak
signposts_triggered.implication: Broadly unchanged and still a supportive risk regime. The prior dossier's risk-appetite assumption remains valid, but the krona has not been rewarded for it, which is the anomaly this dossier flags in Factor 3.

conviction_change.explanation: Tactical conviction is unchanged at 2 but the stance has moved from Neutral to Bearish, so the change is directional rather than one of intensity: the tactical net score moved from plus 0.321 to minus 0.161. Strategic conviction falls from 3 to 2 and the net score from plus 0.474 to plus 0.120 while the Bullish stance is retained. The reduction is driven by three things: the external-balance factor, which carries the second-largest strategic weight at 0.16, moved from Bullish at 68% confidence to Neutral at 53% as the energy shock compressed the trade surplus; Policy and Rates, the largest weight at 0.24, moved from Bullish to Neutral as the level disadvantage widened against a hiking European Central Bank; and Event Risk moved from Neutral to Bearish as the Middle East agreement collapsed and the election moved inside the horizon. The strategic thesis is intact in direction but is now generated by a narrower base, with five factors carrying 63% of the strategic weight registering Neutral.

new_catalysts: The 13 September 2026 Swedish general election has moved from outside the strategic horizon into it, together with the 2027 Budget Bill that follows on the election-year timetable

The expiry dates of the temporary fiscal measures are now inside the strategic window and are the mechanism behind the bullish case: fuel duty on 30 November 2026 and the halved public transport passes on 31 December 2026

Three further tax and subsidy cuts took effect on 1 July 2026 - a deeper fuel duty reduction, a 50% cut to public transport monthly passes and lower preschool fees - which will depress the July CPI prints on 6 and 13 August

Riksgalden's Central Government Borrowing report 2026:1 of 28 May raised nominal bond issuance to SEK 220 billion for 2026 and SEK 240 billion for 2027 and moved to weekly auctions from 17 June, a supply event that was not in the prior dossier

Norges Bank's 13 August meeting is now live, with June guidance that the rate will likely be raised at one of the forthcoming meetings, which would widen the Scandinavian carry deficit to 275 basis points

The United States Section 301 investigations opened in March 2026 into 60 economies including the European Union, and the Section 232 pharmaceutical order effective 31 July 2026, are new trade-policy catalysts affecting 7.7% of Swedish goods exports
The 24 September 2026 Monetary Policy Report is identified as the specific inflection point between the tactical and strategic views, a framing not present in the prior dossier

seasonality.pattern: Two overlapping patterns are relevant. The first is liquidity: July and early August are the thinnest weeks of the Nordic calendar, with the Swedish industrial holiday running through July and market participation returning only in mid-August, which historically amplifies krona moves relative to their fundamental content and widens dealer spreads outside European hours. The second is not a statistical seasonal but a dated fiscal one with the same effect: the Riksbank's June Monetary Policy Report states that temporary fiscal measures reduce CPIF by roughly 1.5 percentage points at their MAXIMUM in the third quarter of 2026, so the measured inflation trough is scheduled to fall inside the tactical window and to reverse inside the strategic one.
seasonality.relevance_window: Both are directly in scope. The liquidity effect runs through August, coinciding with the 6 and 13 August CPI releases and the 20 August Riksbank Update. The fiscal trough peaks in the third quarter and begins reversing with the 30 November fuel duty expiry and the 31 December transport subsidy expiry, both inside the one-to-six-month horizon.
seasonality.historical_magnitude: Not quantified from a published study and stated as a qualitative pattern rather than a measured one. What is measurable is the current volatility state that the liquidity pattern operates on: USD/SEK 20-day realised volatility is 7.80% against 9.87% over 120 days, and EUR/SEK 4.65% against 5.63%, so realised moves are compressed and the tail is fatter than those numbers imply. The fiscal magnitude is quantified by the Riksbank: approximately 1.5 percentage points of CPIF at the Q3 2026 maximum, of which the food VAT cut is roughly 0.8 points, fuel duty up to 0.5 points and halved transport fares just over 0.1 points.
seasonality.current_alignment: Both patterns align with the dossier's tactical-bearish, strategic-bullish structure. Thin August liquidity in a market with a perfectly stacked krona-negative moving-average configuration favours continuation of the existing trend, and the scheduled Q3 inflation trough guarantees that the near-term data flow points the wrong way for the krona before it points the right way. The reversal of the fiscal effect is the mechanism behind the strategic view rather than a coincidence with it.

assumptions: Spot foreign exchange levels are taken from the cycle's Twelve Data price cache at the 31 July 2026 business-day close: USD/SEK 9.51862, with EUR/SEK 10.9783, GBP/SEK 12.8343, NOK/SEK 1.00394, SEK/JPY 16.6539, SEK/CHF 0.08486 and AUD/SEK 6.6963 derived from the same snapshot through the dollar legs. Verification against an independent aggregator returned a 31 July close of USD/SEK 9.6011 and EUR/SEK 11.0101, roughly 0.9% and 0.3% above the cache. The cache is internally consistent - EUR/USD 1.15335 multiplied by USD/SEK 9.51862 reproduces the derived EUR/SEK of 10.9783 exactly - so the divergence is a snapshot-timing difference rather than an error, but readers should treat the spot level as carrying roughly 0.5% of convention uncertainty. FLAGGED.

Performance percentages over 1, 3, 6 and 12 months are computed on calendar-date matching against the nearest available business-day close, not on a fixed trading-day offset. The shared cycle digest used a trading-day-offset convention that produces materially different 6-month and 12-month figures for USD/SEK (plus 2.14% and minus 0.69% respectively, against plus 7.07% and minus 2.63% on the calendar basis used here). The calendar basis is used because it is the correct measure; the discrepancy is noted so that cross-cycle comparisons are made on a like-for-like basis. FLAGGED.

The valuation table is a REER-relative method, not an OECD purchasing power parity table. OECD PPP-based exchange-rate deviations were not retrievable in this cycle, so each currency's June 2026 BIS real broad effective rate is expressed as a deviation from its own mean over the available 30-month window, and the bilateral figure is the Swedish deviation minus the peer deviation. This is the same method used across the other dossiers in this cycle, so the table is internally consistent with them, but it measures deviation from a recent mean rather than from an absolute price level and should not be read as a long-run fair value.

Forward points are derived by covered interest parity, not quoted. Traded krona forward points were not obtainable from any free public venue. The Swedish leg uses STIBOR three-month at 2.04% as fixed on 29 July 2026; the dollar leg uses SOFR at 3.65% on 29 July; the euro leg uses an ESTIMATED three-month Euribor of 2.45%, because the last sourced Euribor fixing of 2.31% dates from 5 June 2026, before the European Central Bank's 25 basis point hike effective 17 June. The euro leg therefore carries roughly plus or minus 10 basis points of uncertainty, which translates to about plus or minus 3 pips on the one-month EUR/SEK forward and plus or minus 18 pips at six months. FLAGGED.

Implied volatility, implied volatility percentiles, 25-delta risk reversals and the volatility term structure are UNOBSERVABLE for the krona complex. No free or public venue publishes an options surface for USD/SEK or EUR/SEK for mid-2026. The iv_1m, iv_3m and iv_percentile_1y fields are therefore null rather than estimated, the vol term structure is recorded as Flat on realised data alone, and no risk-reversal figure is asserted anywhere in the dossier. Carry-to-volatility ratios divide the annualised policy-rate differential in percent by 60-day trailing realised volatility in percent, because three-month implied volatility is unavailable; ratios computed against implied volatility would differ wherever implied exceeds realised.

Positioning data for the Swedish krona does not exist in the CFTC Commitments of Traders report. The Chicago Mercantile Exchange futures-only report for positions as of 28 July 2026 was enumerated in full and contains twelve foreign-exchange contracts, none of which is the Swedish krona or the Norwegian krone. CME Group does list a Swedish Krona SEK/USD product but its open interest is not published in the CFTC release and could not be retrieved. All CFTC numeric fields in this dossier are therefore set to zero to denote absence, and the net speculative percentile of 50 is a structural placeholder meaning no signal rather than a measured reading. Factor 4 confidence of 45 tactical and 50 strategic records this.

The KIX krona index current level could not be sourced. The Riksbank's SWEA statistical interface returns compressed binary that the retrieval tooling cannot decode and its statistics pages are rendered client-side. The National Institute of Economic Research forecast values quoted (119.7 for 2025, 116.2 for 2026 and 116.0 for 2027 on the March vintage; 117.1 and 117.6 on the June vintage) are annual averages read from its published forecast tables, not spot readings. The BIS real broad effective rate of 96.46 for June 2026 is used as the working trade-weighted anchor throughout. FLAGGED.

The current account figure of 4.5% of GDP in the macro comparison table is the OECD quarterly series for the first quarter of 2026, used for cross-currency comparability with the other ten dossiers in this cycle. Statistics Sweden's own presentation of the same quarter is 6.1% of GDP as a four-quarter average, and the National Institute of Economic Research's annual figures are 5.8% for 2025 and 4.7% forecast for 2026. These are three different measures of the same underlying balance and are not in conflict; the OECD quarterly basis is used in the table and the others are cited in the factor analysis where the level matters.

Sweden 5-year sovereign credit default swap levels, the three-month EUR/USD, JPY/USD and SEK/USD cross-currency basis, and the foreign ownership percentage of Swedish government bonds could not be sourced from any free public venue and are stated as gaps rather than estimated. The absence of a cross-currency basis observation is the binding constraint on Factor 10 confidence, because it means an emerging dollar funding squeeze would be visible in the exchange rate before it was visible in the funding market.

Peer policy rates, next meeting dates and macro comparison values are drawn from the shared cycle reference established across the ten dossiers already completed on this 2026-08-01 snapshot, verified against central-bank and tier-one sources during this run. Three items were confirmed as having CHANGED in 2026 and are treated as current rather than legacy: the European Central Bank deposit rate of 2.25% is the result of a hike effective 17 June 2026, the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's 2.50% is the result of a July 2026 hike, and Norges Bank's 4.25% is the result of a 6 May 2026 hike. Two next-meeting dates - the ECB on 10 September and the Monetary Authority of Singapore on 14 October - could not be verified against a primary calendar and are carried from the cycle reference. FLAGGED.

Q2 2026 Swedish GDP of plus 1.4% quarter-on-quarter and plus 2.8% year-on-year is the Statistics Sweden GDP INDICATOR published on 29 July 2026, not the full national accounts, which publish on 28 August 2026. Statistics Sweden itself flags the monthly and indicator outcomes as statistics under development and outside the official statistics. No expenditure composition exists at the valuation date. The quarter also contained one extra working day versus Q2 2025 and June contained two, so part of the year-on-year strength is a calendar artefact; June monthly GDP itself fell 0.2%. The OECD figures of plus 1.37% and plus 2.76% are the same series and are not independent corroboration.

VERIFICATION PASS (Phase 6). An adversarial fact-check was run against the cited sources on 2026-08-02. It confirmed the Riksbank policy rate and June decision, the SCB CPI and GDP prints, the June trade balance, the Riksgalden borrowing programme, the AAA ratings, the BIS REER of 96.46, the OMXS30 close, the Brent and TTF moves, the AP4 disclosures, the election date, and the complete absence of a Swedish krona line in the CFTC report; it also verified both weighted-score tables, all rate and yield spreads, all ten REER-relative fair values and both risk-reward calculations as arithmetically correct, and found no inline provenance tags. It FLAGGED and this dossier has corrected: an incorrect claim that SEK holds the second-lowest policy rate in the G10 (it is the fourth lowest of eleven and third lowest in the G10 proper); a twelve-month high for USD/SEK of 9.7548 that is in fact the 2026 high, the twelve-month high being 9.7759 set on 31 July 2025; a stale superlative on the 10-year yield; and a garbled REER sentence. It flagged as second-hand or vendor-sourced, and these are now labelled as such in the text: the Brent intra-month range, the OMXS30 twelve-month return, the reported 77-83% ECB September hike probability, the Danske dated-hike forecast, the Riksbank quarterly rate-path values (published by the Riksbank only as a chart and reconstructed from Danske's review), and the 10 September ECB and 14 October MAS meeting dates. A Trading Economics terms-of-trade index level was REMOVED rather than flagged because it could not be tied to a primary publisher. BIS and OECD were added to the citation list to cover the REER valuation table and the OECD unemployment, current-account and GDP series. Confidence was lowered on eight of the ten factors as a result: Factor 1 to 63/54, Factor 2 to 58/60, Factor 3 to 52/50, Factor 5 to 52/53, Factor 6 to 58/54, Factor 7 to 50/55, Factor 8 to 57/54, Factor 9 to 56/52 and Factor 10 to 57/55, moving the tactical net score from minus 0.168 to minus 0.161 and the strategic from plus 0.124 to plus 0.120.

Swedish unemployment is reported as 8.9% on the OECD seasonally adjusted basis for June 2026 for cross-country comparability. Statistics Sweden publishes 8.7% on a seasonally adjusted AND trend-smoothed basis and 9.9% unadjusted for the same month. These are the same statistic under different treatments, not competing estimates, and the 0.2 percentage point gap between the OECD and Statistics Sweden figures is a smoothing-method difference.
